hints: Notice $P$ is average output in $\text{W}$ and $S$ is seconds in one day, so the useful energy delivered in one day involves $P$ and $S$.
Recall efficiency is useful output energy divided by total input energy, and the total coal energy supplied in one day involves $N$, $M$ and $E$.
Write the output energy for one day and the input energy for one day, then form output divided by input and compare with the four fractions.
walkthrough: Identify the time period as one day: $N$ is trains per day, $S$ is seconds per day, so work in energy per day.
State the rule: $\text{efficiency} = \frac{\text{useful output energy}}{\text{total input energy}}$.
Useful output energy in one day is power $\times$ time: $E_{out} = P \times S$, in $\text{J}$ since $\text{W} \times \text{s} = \text{J}$.
Total input energy in one day is mass of coal $\times$ energy per kg: mass $= N \times M$ in $\text{kg}$, so $E_{in} = NME$ in $\text{J}$.
Form the ratio $\text{efficiency} = \frac{PS}{NME}$, which is dimensionless as required. This is option A.

options.A: This is $\frac{PS}{NME}$, the useful electrical energy output per day divided by the chemical energy input from coal per day.
options.B: This gives $\frac{PSN}{ME}$ which incorrectly multiplies by $N$ on top, so the number of trains per day is not cancelled correctly.
options.C: This gives $\frac{NME}{PS}$ which is input divided by output, the inverse of efficiency.
options.D: This gives $\frac{NM}{PSE}$ which is inverted and has $E$ in the denominator, giving units of $\text{kg}^2 \text{J}^{-2}$ rather than dimensionless.
